The predicted answer also provides additional names (Wien, Lenard, Lorentz, Zeeman) whose work (within the 1901–1920 laureate list) had relevance to quantum theory, though not always as directly foundational as Planck or Stark.

- Stark’s discovery of the Stark effect is also present in both.
- Einstein and Bohr are mentioned in the predicted answer, with their Nobel Prize years correctly noted as outside the 1901–1920 window (and thus excluded from the main list), echoing the ground truth's inclusion but with a note why they are not strictly part of the direct answer.
- Franck and Hertz are not present in the predicted answer, but their Nobel Prize year (1925) is outside the relevant timeframe.

Therefore, all required laureates and their contributions from the specified period (1901-1920) in the ground truth are present and correctly described in the predicted answer.
